sanskrit: mātāpitror vacanakṛd dhitaḥ pathyaś ca yaḥ sutaḥ sa putraḥ putravad yaś ca vartate pitṛmātṛṣu
english: He who obeys the words of his mother and father, who is devoted and beneficial to them — he is a true son; and he who conducts himself toward his parents as a son should.

sanskrit: yadunāham avajñātas tathā turvasunāpi ca druhyunā cānunā caiva mayy avajñā kṛtā bhṛśam
english: By Yadu I was disrespected, and likewise by Turvasu; by Druhyu and by Anu too, great contempt was shown toward me.

sanskrit: pūruṇā me kṛtaṃ vākyaṃ mānitaś ca viśeṣataḥ kanīyān mama dāyādo jarā yena dhṛtā mama mama kāmaḥ sa ca kṛtaḥ pūruṇā putrarūpiṇā
english: My word was fulfilled by Puru, and I was honored by him especially; he is my youngest heir, he who bore my old age — and my desire was accomplished by Puru, who proved himself a true son.

sanskrit: śukreṇa ca varo dattaḥ kāvyenośanasā svayam putro yas tvānuvarteta sa rājā pṛthivīpatiḥ bhavato 'nunayāmy evaṃ pūrū rājye 'bhiṣicyatām
english: And a boon was granted by Shukra himself, the sage Ushanas Kavya: 'The son who obeys you shall be a king, lord of the earth.' Appealing to you on this ground, let Puru be consecrated to the kingdom.

sanskrit: prakṛtaya ūcuḥ yaḥ putro guṇasaṃpanno mātāpitror hitaḥ sadā sarvam arhati kalyāṇaṃ kanīyān api sa prabho
english: The subjects said: A son who is endowed with virtues and is always devoted to the welfare of his mother and father deserves all prosperity, O lord, even if he is the youngest.

sanskrit: arhaḥ pūrur idaṃ rājyaṃ yaḥ sutaḥ priyakṛt tava varadānena śukrasya na śakyaṃ vaktum uttaram
english: Puru deserves this kingdom; he is the son who has done what pleases you. By virtue of Shukra's boon, there is no reply that can be made against it.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca paurajānapadais tuṣṭair ity ukto nāhuṣas tadā abhyaṣiñcat tataḥ pūruṃ rājye sve sutam ātmajam
english: Vaishampayana said: Thus addressed by the satisfied townspeople and country folk, Nahusha's son at that time anointed his own son Puru in the kingdom.

sanskrit: dattvā ca pūrave rājyaṃ vanavāsāya dīkṣitaḥ purāt sa niryayau rājā brāhmaṇais tāpasaiḥ saha
english: Having given the kingdom to Puru and consecrated himself for forest-dwelling, the king departed from the city accompanied by brahmins and ascetics.

sanskrit: yados tu yādavā jātās turvasor yavanāḥ sutāḥ druhyor api sutā bhojā anos tu mlecchajātayaḥ
english: From Yadu were born the Yadavas; from Turvasu's sons came the Yavanas; from Druhyu's sons came the Bhojas; and from Anu came the tribes of the mlecchas.

sanskrit: pūros tu pauravo vaṃśo yatra jāto 'si pārthiva idaṃ varṣasahasrāya rājyaṃ kārayituṃ vaśī
english: From Puru came the Paurava lineage, in which you were born, O king — he who was master enough to wield the kingdom for a thousand years.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ sa nāhuṣo rājā yayātiḥ putram īpsitam rājye 'bhiṣicya mudito vānaprastho 'bhavan muniḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: Thus king Yayati, son of Nahusha, having joyfully consecrated his desired son to the kingdom, became a forest-dweller and a sage.

sanskrit: uṣitvā ca vane vāsaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha saṃśritaḥ phalamūlāśano dānto mahāśayaḥ yathā svargam ito gataḥ
english: And having dwelt in the forest, taking refuge with brahmins, subsisting on fruits and roots, self-restrained and great-souled, he departed from here to heaven.

sanskrit: sa gataḥ suravāsaṃ taṃ nivasan muditaḥ sukham kālasya nātimahataḥ punaḥ śakreṇa pātitaḥ
english: Having gone to the abode of the gods and dwelling there joyfully and happily, after no very great span of time he was cast down again by Shakra.

sanskrit: nipatan pracyutaḥ svargād aprāpto medinītalam sthita āsīd antarikṣe sa tadeti śrutaṃ mayā
english: Falling, dislodged from heaven, before he could reach the surface of the earth, he stood suspended in mid-air — so I have heard.

sanskrit: tata eva punaś cāpi gataḥ svargam iti śrutiḥ rājñā vasumatā sārdham aṣṭakena ca vīryavān pratardanena śibinā sametya kila saṃsadi
english: And thence he again went to heaven — so goes the tradition — having met, it is said, in an assembly with king Vasumat, with the valiant Ashtaka, with Pratardana, and with Shibi.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca karmaṇā kena sa divaṃ punaḥ prāpto mahīpatiḥ sarvam etad aśeṣeṇa śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ kathyamānaṃ tvayā vipra viprarṣigaṇasaṃnidhau
english: Janamejaya said: By what deed did that lord of the earth once more attain heaven? I wish to hear all of this fully and truly, O brahmin, as related by you in the presence of the assembly of brahmin-sages.

sanskrit: devarājasamo hy āsīd yayātiḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ vardhanaḥ kuruvaṃśasya vibhāvasusamadyutiḥ
english: For Yayati, lord of the earth, was equal to the king of the gods; he was the increaser of the Kuru lineage, blazing with a splendor equal to the sun.

sanskrit: tasya vistīrṇayaśasaḥ satyakīrter mahātmanaḥ caritaṃ śrotum icchāmi divi ceha ca sarvaśaḥ
english: I wish to hear the conduct of that great-souled one of wide-spread fame and true renown — both in heaven and here on earth, in every regard.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi yayāter uttarāṃ kathām divi ceha ca puṇyārthāṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśinīm
english: Vaishampayana said: Very well, I shall tell you the later story of Yayati — meritorious both in heaven and here on earth, and destructive of all sins.

sanskrit: yayātir nāhuṣo rājā pūruṃ putraṃ kanīyasam rājye 'bhiṣicya muditaḥ pravavrāja vanaṃ tadā
english: King Yayati, son of Nahusha, having joyfully consecrated his youngest son Puru to the kingdom, then set forth to the forest.

sanskrit: anteṣu sa vinikṣipya putrān yadupurogamān phalamūlāśano rājā vane saṃnyavasac ciram
english: Having placed his sons led by Yadu on the frontiers, the king, subsisting on fruits and roots, dwelt for a long time in the forest.

sanskrit: saṃśitātmā jitakrodhas tarpayan pitṛdevatāḥ agnīṃś ca vidhivaj juhvan vānaprasthavidhānataḥ
english: With sharpened self, having conquered anger, satisfying the ancestors and the gods, and offering oblations into the sacred fires according to rule, following the ordinances of the forest-dweller stage.

sanskrit: atithīn pūjayām āsa vanyena haviṣā vibhuḥ śiloñchavṛttim āsthāya śeṣānnakṛtabhojanaḥ
english: The mighty one honored guests with forest oblations, following the practice of gleaning fallen grain, eating only what remained after others were fed.

sanskrit: pūrṇaṃ varṣasahasraṃ sa evaṃvṛttir abhūn nṛpaḥ abbhakṣaḥ śaradas triṃśad āsīn niyatavāṅmanāḥ
english: The king maintained this conduct for a full thousand years; for thirty autumns he subsisted on water alone, with restrained speech and mind.

sanskrit: tataś ca vāyubhakṣo 'bhūt saṃvatsaram atandritaḥ pañcāgnimadhye ca tapas tepe saṃvatsaraṃ nṛpaḥ
english: Then he became a subsister on air alone for a year without slackening; and for a year the king performed austerities in the midst of the five fires.

sanskrit: ekapādasthitaś cāsīt ṣaṇ māsān anilāśanaḥ puṇyakīrtis tataḥ svargaṃ jagāmāvṛtya rodasī
english: And he stood on one foot for six months, subsisting on wind; then he of holy fame went to heaven, having pervaded both heaven and earth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca svargataḥ sa tu rājendro nivasan devasadmani pūjitas tridaśaiḥ sādhyair marudbhir vasubhis tathā
english: Vaishampayana said: That foremost of kings, having gone to heaven, dwelling in the abode of the gods, was honored by the Tridasha gods, the Sadhyas, the Maruts, and the Vasus.

sanskrit: devalokād brahmalokaṃ saṃcaran puṇyakṛd vaśī avasat pṛthivīpālo dīrghakālam iti śrutiḥ
english: Moving from the world of the gods to the world of Brahma, that meritorious, self-controlled guardian of the earth dwelt there for a long time — so goes the tradition.

sanskrit: sa kadā cin nṛpaśreṣṭho yayātiḥ śakram āgamat kathānte tatra śakreṇa pṛṣṭaḥ sa pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: At some point that best of kings, Yayati, came to Shakra; and at the end of their conversation, the lord of the earth was questioned by Shakra.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca yadā sa pūrus tava rūpeṇa rājañ; jarāṃ gṛhītvā pracacāra bhūmau tadā rājyaṃ saṃpradāyaiva tasmai; tvayā kim uktaḥ kathayeha satyam
english: Shakra said: When Puru, O king, bearing your old age in your form, roamed the earth, and when you gave the kingdom to him — what did you say to him? Tell me truly.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca gaṅgāyamunayor madhye kṛtsno 'yaṃ viṣayas tava madhye pṛthivyās tvaṃ rājā bhrātaro 'ntyādhipās tava
english: Yayati said: 'All this territory between the Ganga and the Yamuna is yours; you are king in the middle of the earth — your brothers are rulers of the borderlands.'

sanskrit: akrodhanaḥ krodhanebhyo viśiṣṭas; tathā titikṣur atitikṣor viśiṣṭaḥ amānuṣebhyo mānuṣāś ca pradhānā; vidvāṃs tathaivāviduṣaḥ pradhānaḥ
english: 'The one free from anger is superior to the wrathful; likewise the forbearing is superior to the unfor-bearing; humans are paramount over non-humans; and so the wise man is paramount over the ignorant.'

sanskrit: ākruśyamāno nākrośen manyur eva titikṣataḥ ākroṣṭāraṃ nirdahati sukṛtaṃ cāsya vindati
english: 'When reviled, one should not revile in return — the patient man's anger alone burns up the reviler, and he himself gains merit.'

sanskrit: nāruṃtudaḥ syān na nṛśaṃsavādī; na hīnataḥ param abhyādadīta yayāsya vācā para udvijeta; na tāṃ vaced ruśatīṃ pāpalokyām
english: 'One should not be wounding, nor speak cruelly; one should not seize upon another's weakness. The speech that causes another to tremble — one should not utter that harsh word that leads to evil worlds.'

sanskrit: aruṃtudaṃ puruṣaṃ rūkṣavācaṃ; vākkaṇṭakair vitudantaṃ manuṣyān vidyād alakṣmīkatamaṃ janānāṃ; mukhe nibaddhāṃ nirṛtiṃ vahantam
english: 'A man who is wounding, harsh of speech, piercing people with the thorns of his words — know him to be the most inauspicious of people, bearing destruction bound to his mouth.'

sanskrit: sadbhiḥ purastād abhipūjitaḥ syāt; sadbhis tathā pṛṣṭhato rakṣitaḥ syāt sadāsatām ativādāṃs titikṣet; satāṃ vṛttaṃ cādadītāryavṛttaḥ
english: 'One should be honored by the good from the front and protected by the good from behind; one should always forbear the excessive speech of the wicked; and conducting oneself nobly, one should adopt the conduct of the good.'

sanskrit: vāksāyakā vadanān niṣpatanti; yair āhataḥ śocati rātryahāni parasya vā marmasu ye patanti; tān paṇḍito nāvasṛjet pareṣu
english: 'Word-arrows fly forth from the mouth; struck by them, one grieves through nights and days. When they strike another's vital spots — a wise man should never discharge such words at others.'

sanskrit: na hīdṛśaṃ saṃvananaṃ triṣu lokeṣu vidyate yathā maitrī ca bhūteṣu dānaṃ ca madhurā ca vāk
english: 'Indeed there is no means of winning over others in the three worlds like friendliness toward all beings, giving, and sweet speech.'

sanskrit: tasmāt sāntvaṃ sadā vācyaṃ na vācyaṃ paruṣaṃ kva cit pūjyān saṃpūjayed dadyān na ca yācet kadā cana
english: 'Therefore one should always speak gently and never speak harshly anywhere; one should honor those worthy of honor; one should give and never beg.'

sanskrit: indra uvāca sarvāṇi karmāṇi samāpya rājan; gṛhān parityajya vanaṃ gato 'si tat tvāṃ pṛcchāmi nahuṣasya putra; kenāsi tulyas tapasā yayāte
english: Indra said: Having completed all your duties, O king, you abandoned your home and went to the forest. This I ask you, O son of Nahusha — with whose austerity are you equal, O Yayati?

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca nāhaṃ devamanuṣyeṣu na gandharvamaharṣiṣu ātmanas tapasā tulyaṃ kaṃ cit paśyāmi vāsava
english: Yayati said: I see no one equal to myself in austerity — not among gods and men, not among gandharvas and great sages, O Vasava.

sanskrit: indra uvāca yadāvamaṃsthāḥ sadṛśaḥ śreyasaś ca; pāpīyasaś cāviditaprabhāvaḥ tasmāl lokā antavantas taveme; kṣīṇe puṇye patitāsy adya rājan
english: Indra said: Because you held in contempt those equal to you and even superior to you, not knowing their power — therefore your worlds are now finite; your merit exhausted, you have fallen today, O king.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca surarṣigandharvanarāvamānāt; kṣayaṃ gatā me yadi śakra lokāḥ iccheyaṃ vai suralokād vihīnaḥ; satāṃ madhye patituṃ devarāja
english: Yayati said: If my worlds are exhausted, O Shakra, by having shown contempt for gods, sages, gandharvas, and men — then I wish, though bereft of the heavenly world, to fall among the good, O king of the gods.

sanskrit: indra uvāca satāṃ sakāśe patitāsi rājaṃś; cyutaḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ yatra labdhāsi bhūyaḥ evaṃ viditvā tu punar yayāte; na te 'vamānyāḥ sadṛśaḥ śreyasaś ca
english: Indra said: You have fallen in the presence of the good, O king; having fallen, you will regain your footing once more. Knowing this, O Yayati, do not again despise those equal to you and those superior to you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ prahāyāmararājajuṣṭān; puṇyāṃl lokān patamānaṃ yayātim saṃprekṣya rājarṣivaro 'ṣṭakas tam; uvāca saddharmavidhānagoptā
english: Vaishampayana said: Then, seeing Yayati falling, having abandoned the blessed worlds cherished by the king of immortals, the foremost royal sage Ashtaka, guardian of the ordinances of right conduct, spoke to him.

sanskrit: kas tvaṃ yuvā vāsavatulyarūpaḥ; svatejasā dīpyamāno yathāgniḥ patasy udīrṇāmbudharāndhakārāt; khāt khecarāṇāṃ pravaro yathārkaḥ
english: 'Who are you, youthful and equal in form to Vasava, blazing with your own splendor like fire, falling from the sky out of the darkness of rising storm-clouds, like the sun, supreme among sky-travellers?'

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca tvāṃ sūryapathāt patantaṃ; vaiśvānarārkadyutim aprameyam kiṃ nu svid etat patatīti sarve; vitarkayantaḥ parimohitāḥ smaḥ
english: 'Seeing you falling from the path of the sun, your immeasurable radiance like fire and the sun, all of us, speculating what indeed is this that falls, are utterly bewildered.'

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca tvāṃ viṣṭhitaṃ devamārge; śakrārkaviṣṇupratimaprabhāvam abhyudgatās tvāṃ vayam adya sarve; tattvaṃ pāte tava jijñāsamānāḥ
english: 'And seeing you stationed in the path of the gods, with power equal to Shakra, the sun, and Vishnu, all of us have come forward today to meet you, desiring to know the truth of your fall.'

sanskrit: na cāpi tvāṃ dhṛṣṇumaḥ praṣṭum agre; na ca tvam asmān pṛcchasi ye vayaṃ smaḥ tat tvāṃ pṛcchāmaḥ spṛhaṇīyarūpaṃ; kasya tvaṃ vā kiṃnimittaṃ tvam āgāḥ
english: 'We did not dare to question you first, and you do not ask us who we are. So we ask you of desirable form: whose son are you? And for what reason have you come?'

sanskrit: bhayaṃ tu te vyetu viṣādamohau; tyajāśu devendrasamānarūpa tvāṃ vartamānaṃ hi satāṃ sakāśe; nālaṃ prasoḍhuṃ balahāpi śakraḥ
english: 'But let fear depart from you; abandon grief and confusion quickly, O you of form equal to the lord of gods — for while you remain in the presence of the good, even Shakra, the slayer of Bala, is not able to harm you.'

sanskrit: santaḥ pratiṣṭhā hi sukhacyutānāṃ; satāṃ sadaivāmararājakalpa te saṃgatāḥ sthāvarajaṅgameśāḥ; pratiṣṭitas tvaṃ sadṛśeṣu satsu
english: 'For the good are truly the foundation for those dislodged from happiness; the good are always like the king of immortals. Those lords of the moving and unmoving are gathered here; you stand firm among the good who are your equals.'

sanskrit: prabhur agniḥ pratapane bhūmir āvapane prabhuḥ prabhuḥ sūryaḥ prakāśitve satāṃ cābhyāgataḥ prabhuḥ
english: 'Fire is lord in burning, earth is lord in sustaining, the sun is lord in illuminating — and one who has come to the good is lord.'

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca ahaṃ yayātir nahuṣasya putraḥ; pūroḥ pitā sarvabhūtāvamānāt prabhraṃśitaḥ surasiddharṣilokāt; paricyutaḥ prapatāmy alpapuṇyaḥ
english: Yayati said: I am Yayati, son of Nahusha, father of Puru; through contempt for all beings I have been cast down from the worlds of gods, siddhas, and sages; having fallen away, I fall, my merit exhausted.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi pūrvo vayasā bhavadbhyas; tenābhivādaṃ bhavatāṃ na prayuñje yo vidyayā tapasā janmanā vā; vṛddhaḥ sa pūjyo bhavati dvijānām
english: 'I am older in age than all of you; therefore I do not offer salutation to you — for he who is elder by learning, austerity, or birth is worthy of worship among the twice-born.'

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca avādīś ced vayasā yaḥ sa vṛddha; iti rājan nābhyavadaḥ kathaṃ cit yo vai vidvān vayasā san sma vṛddhaḥ; sa eva pūjyo bhavati dvijānām
english: Ashtaka said: If you said that he who is elder in years is the elder, O king, then you should have saluted us in some manner — for he who is truly wise and elder in years is the one worthy of worship among the twice-born.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca pratikūlaṃ karmaṇāṃ pāpam āhus; tad vartate 'pravaṇe pāpalokyam santo 'satāṃ nānuvartanti caitad; yathā ātmaiṣām anukūlavādī
english: Yayati said: They call sin the course contrary to right action; it dwells in one inclined toward evil worlds. The good do not go along with the wicked in this, like a self that speaks in accordance with what is agreeable to them.

sanskrit: abhūd dhanaṃ me vipulaṃ mahad vai; viceṣṭamāno nādhigantā tad asmi evaṃ pradhāryātmahite niviṣṭo; yo vartate sa vijānāti jīvan
english: 'My wealth was immense and great; yet striving I could not retain it. He who, having reflected thus and fixed his mind on his own welfare, conducts himself accordingly — he truly knows how to live.'

sanskrit: nānābhāvā bahavo jīvaloke; daivādhīnā naṣṭaceṣṭādhikārāḥ tat tat prāpya na vihanyeta dhīro; diṣṭaṃ balīya iti matvātmabuddhyā
english: 'Many and various are the states of existence in the world of the living, governed by fate, with their efforts and powers lost. Encountering each such state, the wise man should not be distressed, thinking with steady mind: fate is supreme.'

sanskrit: sukhaṃ hi jantur yadi vāpi duḥkhaṃ; daivādhīnaṃ vindati nātmaśaktyā tasmād diṣṭaṃ balavan manyamāno; na saṃjvaren nāpi hṛṣyet kadā cit
english: 'Whether a creature obtains happiness or suffering, it is under the control of fate, not by its own power. Therefore, holding fate to be supreme, one should neither burn with grief nor ever exult.'

sanskrit: duḥkhe na tapyen na sukhena hṛṣyet; samena varteta sadaiva dhīraḥ diṣṭaṃ balīya iti manyamāno; na saṃjvaren nāpi hṛṣyet kadā cit
english: 'The wise man should not be tormented by sorrow nor exult in happiness; he should always conduct himself with equanimity, thinking fate to be supreme — he should neither burn with grief nor ever exult.'

sanskrit: bhaye na muhyāmy aṣṭakāhaṃ kadā cit; saṃtāpo me mānaso nāsti kaś cit dhātā yathā māṃ vidadhāti loke; dhruvaṃ tathāhaṃ bhaviteti matvā
english: 'I am never deluded by fear, O Ashtaka; there is no mental anguish in me whatsoever, thinking: as the Creator ordains my existence in the world, so certainly shall I be.'

sanskrit: saṃsvedajā aṇḍajā udbhidāś ca; sarīsṛpāḥ kṛmayo 'thāpsu matsyāḥ tathāśmānas tṛṇakāṣṭhaṃ ca sarvaṃ; diṣṭakṣaye svāṃ prakṛtiṃ bhajante
english: 'Creatures born from sweat, born from eggs, and those that sprout from the earth; reptiles, worms, fish in the waters; stones, grass, and wood — all at the exhaustion of their ordained span return to their own nature.'

sanskrit: anityatāṃ sukhaduḥkhasya buddhvā; kasmāt saṃtāpam aṣṭakāhaṃ bhajeyam kiṃ kuryāṃ vai kiṃ ca kṛtvā na tapye; tasmāt saṃtāpaṃ varjayāmy apramattaḥ
english: 'Understanding the impermanence of pleasure and pain, why should I, O Ashtaka, indulge in anguish? What shall I do, and having done what shall I not grieve? Therefore, vigilant, I abandon all anguish.'

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca ye ye lokāḥ pārthivendra pradhānās; tvayā bhuktā yaṃ ca kālaṃ yathā ca tan me rājan brūhi sarvaṃ yathāvat; kṣetrajñavad bhāṣase tvaṃ hi dharmān
english: Ashtaka said: What worlds, O foremost of earthly kings, were the chief ones you enjoyed, and for how long, and in what manner? Tell me all of this, O king, exactly as it was — for you speak of dharma like one who knows the field.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca rājāham āsam iha sārvabhaumas; tato lokān mahato ajayaṃ vai tatrāvasaṃ varṣasahasramātraṃ; tato lokaṃ param asmy abhyupetaḥ
english: Yayati said: I was here a universal sovereign of all the earth; then I won great worlds. I dwelt there for just a thousand years; then I advanced to a higher world.

sanskrit: tataḥ purīṃ puruhūtasya ramyāṃ; sahasradvārāṃ śatayojanāyatām adhyāvasaṃ varṣasahasramātraṃ; tato lokaṃ param asmy abhyupetaḥ
english: Then in the delightful city of Puruhuta — with a thousand gates, extending a hundred yojanas — I dwelt for just a thousand years; then I advanced to a higher world.

sanskrit: tato divyam ajaraṃ prāpya lokaṃ; prajāpater lokapater durāpam tatrāvasaṃ varṣasahasramātraṃ; tato lokaṃ param asmy abhyupetaḥ
english: Then having attained the divine, ageless world of Prajapati, lord of worlds — difficult to reach — I dwelt there for just a thousand years; then I advanced to a higher world.

sanskrit: devasya devasya niveśane ca; vijitya lokān avasaṃ yatheṣṭam saṃpūjyamānas tridaśaiḥ samastais; tulyaprabhāvadyutir īśvarāḥ
english: And in the dwelling of god after god, having won the worlds, I dwelt as I pleased, honored by all the Tridasha gods, equal in power and splendor to the lords.

sanskrit: tathāvasaṃ nandane kāmarūpī; saṃvatsarāṇām ayutaṃ śatānām sahāpsarobhir viharan puṇyagandhān; paśyan nagān puṣpitāṃś cārurūpān
english: And thus I dwelt in Nandana, taking whatever form I desired, for a hundred times ten thousand years, roaming with the apsaras, smelling the sacred fragrances, beholding the flowering trees of beautiful form.

sanskrit: tatrasthaṃ māṃ devasukheṣu saktaṃ; kāle 'tīte mahati tato 'timātram dūto devānām abravīd ugrarūpo; dhvaṃsety uccais triḥ plutena svareṇa
english: When I was stationed there, absorbed in the pleasures of the gods, after a very great time had passed, a messenger of the gods of terrible form cried out loudly three times in a prolonged voice: 'Fall!'

sanskrit: etāvan me viditaṃ rājasiṃha; tato bhraṣṭo 'haṃ nandanāt kṣīṇapuṇyaḥ vāco 'śrauṣaṃ cāntarikṣe surāṇām; anukrośāc chocatāṃ mānavendra
english: This is all that I know, O lion among kings; then I fell from Nandana, my merit exhausted. And I heard the voices of the gods in the sky, lamenting with compassion, O lord of men.

sanskrit: aho kaṣṭaṃ kṣīṇapuṇyo yayātiḥ; pataty asau puṇyakṛt puṇyakīrtiḥ tān abruvaṃ patamānas tato 'haṃ; satāṃ madhye nipateyaṃ kathaṃ nu
english: 'Alas, how painful — Yayati, whose merit is exhausted, he who wrought merit and had a holy name, is falling.' Then I, while falling, said to them: 'How might I fall among the good?'

sanskrit: tair ākhyātā bhavatāṃ yajñabhūmiḥ; samīkṣya caināṃ tvaritam upāgato 'smi havirgandhaṃ deśikaṃ yajñabhūmer; dhūmāpāṅgaṃ pratigṛhya pratītaḥ
english: By them was this sacrificial ground of yours pointed out to me; perceiving it, I came here swiftly, guided by the fragrance of the oblations of this sacrificial ground, following the trail of the smoke with confidence.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca yadāvaso nandane kāmarūpī; saṃvatsarāṇām ayutaṃ śatānām kiṃ kāraṇaṃ kārtayugapradhāna; hitvā tattvaṃ vasudhām anvapadyaḥ
english: Ashtaka said: When you dwelt in Nandana taking whatever form you desired, for a hundred times ten thousand years — what was the reason, O foremost one of the Krita age, that abandoning that estate you descended to the earth?

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca jñātiḥ suhṛt svajano yo yatheha; kṣīṇe vitte tyajyate mānavair hi tathā tatra kṣīṇapuṇyaṃ manuṣyaṃ; tyajanti sadyaḥ seśvarā devasaṃghāḥ
english: Yayati said: Just as here a kinsman, friend, or companion is abandoned by people when his wealth is exhausted — so there, when a person's merit is exhausted, the assemblies of gods together with their lords abandon him at once.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca kathaṃ tasmin kṣīṇapuṇyā bhavanti; saṃmuhyate me 'tra mano 'timātram kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ kasya dhāmopayānti; tad vai brūhi kṣetravit tvaṃ mato me
english: Ashtaka said: How does their merit become exhausted in that place? My mind is greatly bewildered on this point. What are their characteristics, and to whose abode do they go? Tell me that indeed — you are regarded by me as one who knows the field.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca imaṃ bhaumaṃ narakaṃ te patanti; lālapyamānā naradeva sarve te kaṅkagomāyubalāśanārthaṃ; kṣīṇā vivṛddhiṃ bahudhā vrajanti
english: Yayati said: They all fall into this earthly hell, O lord of men, lamenting. Exhausted, as food for herons, jackals, and vultures, they go in many directions to grow again.

sanskrit: tasmād etad varjanīyaṃ nareṇa; duṣṭaṃ loke garhaṇīyaṃ ca karma ākhyātaṃ te pārthiva sarvam etad; bhūyaś cedānīṃ vada kiṃ te vadāmi
english: 'Therefore this corrupted and censurable action in the world is to be avoided by a man. All of this has been told to you, O king; say now what more I may tell you.'

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca yadā tu tān vitudante vayāṃsi; tathā gṛdhrāḥ śitikaṇṭhāḥ pataṃgāḥ kathaṃ bhavanti katham ābhavanti; na bhaumam anyaṃ narakaṃ śṛṇomi
english: Ashtaka said: When the birds peck at them — vultures, blue-necked herons, and insects — how do they come to be, how do they come into existence? I hear of no other hell than this earthly one.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca ūrdhvaṃ dehāt karmaṇo jṛmbhamāṇād; vyaktaṃ pṛthivyām anusaṃcaranti imaṃ bhaumaṃ narakaṃ te patanti; nāvekṣante varṣapūgān anekān
english: Yayati said: Rising upward from the body as karma expands, they clearly wander upon the earth; they fall into this earthly hell and do not look back for many, many years.
